High disruption combined with low demand elasticity therefore points to significant headcount pressure and a shift toward oversight and complex cases.

title: Medical scientists
rationale: AI will substantially reshape literature review, hypothesis generation, experimental design, biomedical data analysis, drug discovery, grant writing, and publication, although laboratory experiments, clinical validation, safety oversight, and scientific judgment still require significant human involvement. Demand is highly elastic because cheaper and faster research would enable more disease targets, drug candidates, personalized therapies, and studies than current budgets and researcher capacity permit. Aging populations, chronic disease, and large unmet medical needs reinforce this latent demand, though laboratory and regulatory bottlenecks prevent an even higher score. Thus, medical scientists are likely to become far more productive and work differently, while expanding research activity supports stable or growing employment.

title: Medical transcriptionists
rationale: The occupation consists almost entirely of routine digital language processing—transcribing, formatting, checking, and entering dictated medical information—which speech recognition and generative AI increasingly perform directly. Human review remains valuable for ambiguous audio, clinical inconsistencies, legal compliance, and patient-safety risks, but improved models will reduce the amount of review required per document. Demand is highly inelastic because documentation volume is largely tied to the number of patient encounters, and cheaper transcription will not produce substantially more encounters or reports. Consequently, productivity gains will allow fewer transcriptionists to handle the existing workload, making replacement the most likely net effect.

title: Meeting, convention, and event planners
rationale: AI can substantially accelerate venue research, budgeting, scheduling, vendor comparisons, communications, contract review, registration, and attendee feedback analysis. However, client relationship management, venue inspection, negotiation, vendor coordination, and real-time handling of unpredictable event problems still require human judgment and physical presence. Lower planning costs could make professional services accessible for more small events, but demand is constrained by the number of events and by venue, catering, travel, and entertainment costs. The occupation is therefore resilient, with AI improving productivity and reducing administrative workload without fully reshaping its presence-intensive core.

title: Metal and plastic machine workers
rationale: AI will improve CNC programming, machine setup, predictive maintenance, process optimization, and automated visual inspection, while enabling one operator to oversee more equipment. However, loading materials, changing tools, handling irregular parts, troubleshooting machinery, and working safely around physical production systems still require substantial on-site labor and mechanical skill. Demand is relatively inelastic because it is derived from demand for manufactured parts and finished goods, so lower production costs will increase output only modestly and may primarily reduce labor per unit. The occupation is therefore resilient under the specified taxonomy because disruption remains moderate, although conventional robotics and automation will continue to reduce operator headcount and shift jobs toward programming, setup, and maintenance.

title: Microbiologists
rationale: AI will substantially assist literature review, experimental design, genomic and imaging analysis, microorganism classification, and technical writing. However, core duties still involve physical sample handling, culturing organisms, operating laboratory equipment, enforcing biosafety procedures, and interpreting uncertain experimental results in real-world contexts. Cheaper and faster research could support more drug discovery, diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and industrial biotechnology, but funding, regulation, laboratory capacity, and biological testing cycles limit demand expansion. Because AI reshapes the analytical portions without replacing the hands-on experimental core, the occupation remains resilient.

title: Middle school teachers
rationale: AI will substantially assist with lesson planning, grading, assessment design, parent communications, and personalized instructional materials. However, classroom management, student supervision, motivation, social-emotional support, and real-time adaptation to adolescents still require a trusted human presence. Demand is constrained by student enrollment, class sizes, licensing rules, and public-school budgets, so greater productivity is unlikely to generate proportionally more teaching services. Because AI reshapes many supporting tasks without replacing the occupation's in-person core, the occupation is resilient.

title: Military careers
rationale: Military careers span physical combat, field operations, maintenance, leadership, healthcare, logistics, and digital intelligence, so AI will substantially alter planning, surveillance, administration, and some technical specialties but cannot replace much of the required real-world presence and human command authority. Autonomous systems may reduce personnel needs in selected roles, while creating new work in cyber operations, robotics, electronic warfare, and AI oversight. Total personnel demand is relatively inelastic because it is set primarily by national-security strategy, force-readiness requirements, and congressional budgets rather than the market price of individual military services. The occupation is therefore resilient overall, although disruption will vary sharply across specialties.

title: Mining and geological engineers
rationale: AI will materially improve geological modeling, mine design optimization, production monitoring, hazard detection, and technical reporting. However, core responsibilities still require site-specific judgment, field inspections, coordination of physical operations, regulatory accountability, and safety-critical decisions in unpredictable environments. Demand is derived mainly from mineral production and the number of viable mining projects, so cheaper engineering may enable some additional exploration and optimization but will not generate proportionate growth in projects. With moderate disruption and limited demand elasticity, the occupation is resilient, although workflows and staffing within engineering teams will change.

title: Models
rationale: Generative imagery, digital avatars, virtual try-on systems, and image-reuse tools can substitute for human models in much of the high-volume advertising, catalog, and online retail market. Runway shows, fitting work, live promotions, and artist sessions still require physical presence, preventing an even higher disruption score. Cheaper content will increase the number and variety of promotional images, but much of that expansion will use synthetic models rather than create additional human assignments, so demand for human-model headcount is relatively inelastic and the net effect is replacement.

title: Music directors and composers
rationale: Generative music systems can already produce drafts, arrangements, orchestrations, lyrics, and synthetic recordings, putting much of composers’ digital creative workflow directly in AI’s path. Music directors are less exposed because conducting rehearsals, interpreting performances, leading musicians, and maintaining community relationships require real-time human presence and trust. Lower production costs will expand demand for customized music across video, games, advertising, and online media, but audience attention, arts funding, and the number of live ensembles constrain how much additional employment results. The occupation therefore faces substantial skill and workflow changes, while only moderate demand expansion makes restructure the best fit.

title: Musicians and singers
rationale: Generative AI can produce recordings, backing tracks, synthetic vocals, promotional content, and practice aids, materially changing studio work and career management. However, live performance, auditions, rehearsals, physical technique, and audience connection remain embodied activities in which the human performer is often the product. Lower production costs will generate substantially more music and personalized content, although limited listener attention and substitution by fully synthetic music constrain demand for paid human performers. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high across the occupation's core performance tasks, the occupation fits the resilient category.

title: Natural sciences managers
rationale: AI will materially accelerate literature review, experimental analysis, reporting, budgeting, scheduling, and project monitoring. However, scientific judgment, regulatory accountability, laboratory oversight, strategic prioritization, and the hiring and leadership of specialized teams remain strongly human-centered. Cheaper and faster research should stimulate additional R&D and product development, but funding constraints, laboratory capacity, regulation, and flexible manager-to-staff ratios limit headcount expansion. Because AI substantially assists rather than overtakes the occupation's core leadership and real-world coordination functions, the occupation is resilient.

title: Network and computer systems administrators
rationale: Most administration tasks are digital and increasingly automatable through AI-assisted troubleshooting, infrastructure-as-code, autonomous monitoring, cloud platforms, and managed network services. Physical installation, organization-specific integration, security accountability, and response to unusual outages still require skilled humans, but the role will shift from routine maintenance toward automation, architecture, governance, and incident management. Lower administration costs will support more infrastructure and stronger security, yet demand expansion is constrained because organizations need only a limited number of administrators and can consolidate work through cloud and service providers. High disruption combined with moderate elasticity therefore points to restructuring, with fewer traditional administrators but continued demand for workers who master cloud, DevOps, security, and AI-enabled operations.

title: News analysts, reporters, and journalists
rationale: AI can materially accelerate research, transcription, drafting, editing, fact comparison, multimedia production, and adaptation of stories across platforms. However, source development, field reporting, original investigation, interviews, verification, and trusted public presence still require substantial human judgment and relationships. Cheaper production may support more niche and personalized coverage, but audience attention, advertising revenue, and willingness to pay limit how much additional journalism can be monetized. The occupation therefore faces restructuring toward verification, investigation, source cultivation, and AI-assisted multimedia work, with fewer roles centered mainly on routine content production.

title: Nuclear engineers
rationale: Much of nuclear engineering consists of computer-based modeling, simulation, design optimization, technical writing, data analysis, and regulatory review, all of which AI can materially accelerate. Physical inspections, experiments, facility-specific judgment, security requirements, and legally accountable safety decisions limit full automation, but the core workflow will still change substantially. Demand is constrained by the small number of nuclear facilities, long construction timelines, regulation, and capital costs, so cheaper engineering is unlikely to generate proportionate growth in projects. High disruption combined with low demand elasticity therefore points to headcount pressure and consolidation of work among AI-enabled engineers.

title: Nuclear medicine technologists
rationale: Core tasks require in-person patient care, physical preparation and administration of radiopharmaceuticals, equipment operation, and strict radiation-safety procedures that AI cannot readily perform autonomously. AI can improve scheduling, documentation, dose calculation, image acquisition, quality control, and protocol selection, but these are primarily assistive changes. Lower costs could modestly increase imaging and treatment volumes, especially as the population ages, but clinical indications, radiation exposure limits, regulation, equipment capacity, and radiopharmaceutical supply constrain demand. The occupation is therefore resilient because AI affects peripheral and technical workflow components without replacing its hands-on core.

title: Nuclear technicians
rationale: AI can materially improve sensor analysis, anomaly detection, calculations, documentation, and decontamination planning. However, core duties also require onsite sampling, equipment calibration and maintenance, incident response, and accountable safety oversight in tightly regulated facilities. Demand is tied mainly to the number of nuclear plants, laboratories, and waste sites, so cheaper monitoring would generate little additional work. The occupation is therefore resilient to wholesale replacement, although its analytical and control-room tasks will become increasingly AI-assisted.

title: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners
rationale: AI will materially assist with documentation, diagnostic interpretation, care planning, monitoring, and patient education, but physical examinations, procedures, anesthesia administration, childbirth, and real-time clinical judgment still require licensed human presence. Demand is relatively elastic because aging, chronic disease, provider shortages, and unmet primary-care needs mean that lower-cost, more productive APRN services would enable substantially more care, although regulation and facility capacity limit expansion. Because AI reshapes the cognitive and administrative portions without replacing the occupation's hands-on, accountable clinical core, the occupation is resilient.

title: Nursing assistants and orderlies
rationale: Most core tasks involve hands-on personal care, patient movement, cleaning, observation, and empathetic interaction in unpredictable clinical environments. AI can improve documentation, monitoring, communication, scheduling, and care coordination, while robotics may assist with transport and lifting, but neither is likely to replace most bedside work within a decade. Cheaper care would unlock meaningful demand from an aging population and underserved home- and community-based settings, although reimbursement and facility budgets constrain expansion. Because disruption remains low despite moderate demand elasticity, the occupation is resilient.

title: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians
rationale: AI can automate regulatory research, incident-data analysis, report drafting, training materials, and sensor or computer-vision monitoring. However, inspections, equipment testing, emergency response, worker education, and investigations in varied and hazardous worksites still require substantial human presence and judgment. Lower costs could enable more frequent assessments and make professional safety programs accessible to smaller employers, although regulation and the finite number of workplaces limit expansion. Because AI materially improves the analytical portions without replacing the field-based core, the occupation remains resilient.

title: Occupational therapists
rationale: AI can assist with documentation, progress tracking, treatment-plan drafting, equipment recommendations, and analysis of sensor or video data. However, core tasks require in-person observation, hands-on demonstration, adaptation to individual limitations and environments, and trusted interaction with clients and families. Demand could expand meaningfully because of population aging and unmet rehabilitation needs, although licensure, reimbursement, and the time-intensive nature of treatment limit elasticity. Occupational therapy is therefore resilient: AI will improve clinical and administrative workflows without substantially replacing therapists' central role.

title: Occupational therapy assistants and aides
rationale: Core duties require in-person guidance, physical assistance, equipment setup, observation, and empathetic interaction with clients, making them difficult to automate with AI. AI can streamline documentation, scheduling, insurance paperwork, progress tracking, and treatment suggestions, but these are supporting rather than defining tasks. Cheaper delivery could expand access amid an aging population and unmet rehabilitation needs, although insurance reimbursement, licensing, supervision, and facility capacity limit the expansion. Because disruption remains low despite moderate demand elasticity, the occupation is resilient.

title: Oil and gas workers
rationale: Core duties involve physical equipment operation, maintenance, repair, and material handling in hazardous, unpredictable worksites, putting most tasks beyond near-term AI capabilities. AI-enabled remote monitoring, predictive maintenance, and automated drilling will reduce some inspection and control work, but robotics rather than software alone would be required to replace most workers. Demand is relatively inelastic because oil and gas output is constrained by energy consumption, commodity markets, geology, regulation, and capital investment rather than labor cost alone. The occupation is therefore resilient to AI, although continued automation may limit employment growth and shift workers toward maintenance and oversight.

title: Operations research analysts
rationale: Nearly all core tasks are digital and cognitive, and AI can already accelerate data preparation, model formulation, coding, scenario testing, and report writing. Human analysts remain important for framing ambiguous problems, validating assumptions, incorporating operational constraints, and persuading decision-makers. Lower costs should unlock substantial latent demand as more organizations and business functions apply optimization to pricing, logistics, scheduling, and resource allocation. Thus, the occupation will change substantially, but expanded use of analytics is likely to absorb much of the productivity gain, supporting an augment classification.

title: Opticians
rationale: AI, virtual try-on systems, automated facial measurements, and recommendation tools can streamline frame selection, prescription processing, sales, and inventory work. However, precise fitting, physical adjustments and repairs, contact-lens instruction, and in-person customer service still require dexterity and real-world presence. Demand is relatively inelastic because eyewear purchases are driven mainly by prescriptions, replacement cycles, and demographics rather than the cost of optician labor. AI will alter peripheral sales and administrative tasks, but the occupation's hands-on core makes it resilient.

title: Optometrists
rationale: AI will materially improve image interpretation, diagnostic triage, documentation, treatment planning, and routine refractive testing. However, optometrists still perform hands-on examinations and procedures, validate findings, manage complex conditions, counsel patients, and carry licensed clinical responsibility. Lower costs could expand screening and access somewhat, but visit frequency is constrained by clinical need, regulation, and population size. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, AI is likely to augment clinical practice without fundamentally displacing the occupation.

title: Orthotists and prosthetists
rationale: AI-assisted imaging, biomechanical modeling, digital design, and automated fabrication will materially streamline measurement and device production. However, patient evaluation, hands-on fitting, physical adjustment, counseling, and clinical judgment require in-person expertise and remain central to the occupation. Lower costs could improve access and enable more frequent customization, but demand is constrained by the incidence of relevant medical conditions, prescriptions, and insurance coverage. The occupation is therefore resilient because AI will improve important workflows without replacing its core patient-facing and manual responsibilities.

title: Painters, construction and maintenance
rationale: The core work is physical and site-specific, involving surface preparation, masking, climbing, detailed application, and adaptation to irregular or hazardous environments. AI can improve estimating, scheduling, color visualization, customer communication, and quality inspection, while robotic painting will remain concentrated in standardized industrial settings. If painting became much cheaper, demand would rise through less do-it-yourself work, more frequent repainting, and wider use of protective coatings, although the stock of paintable surfaces limits expansion. Because AI is unlikely to reshape most hands-on tasks over the next decade, the occupation is resilient.

title: Painting and coating workers
rationale: The occupation is dominated by physical tasks such as surface preparation, equipment setup, coating application, inspection, touch-up, and maintenance. AI-enabled robotics, computer vision, and process controls will further automate standardized factory lines, but varied products, repair work, and hard-to-reach surfaces will continue to require hands-on workers. Demand is relatively inelastic because coating needs are tied mainly to the number of goods manufactured or repaired, so lower costs would produce only modest additional usage. With moderate rather than high AI disruption, the occupation is resilient, although employment may remain constrained by broader industrial automation.

title: Paralegals and legal assistants
rationale: Most core tasks—legal research, document review, drafting, summarization, file organization, and case analysis—are digital and already materially accelerated by AI. Human verification, client interaction, court procedures, and trial support remain important, but they represent a smaller or less automatable share of the occupation. Lower costs may unlock some additional legal work, especially for small firms and underserved clients, but attorney supervision, regulation, litigation volumes, and client budgets constrain demand expansion. With very high disruption and low elasticity, productivity gains are likely to reduce paralegal headcount even as remaining roles become more supervisory and client-facing.

title: Personal financial advisors
rationale: Portfolio analysis, financial-plan generation, account monitoring, investment research, and routine client education are digital cognitive tasks that AI and robo-advisors can increasingly automate. Human advisors remain important for trust, sales, regulatory accountability, behavioral coaching, and complex life events, but AI will substantially change their workflows and reduce time spent on analysis and documentation. Lower costs could extend personalized advice to more middle-income households and support larger client books, although limited investable assets, regulation, and preferences for self-service automation constrain headcount expansion. The result is restructuring: fewer purely analytical or transactional roles and greater emphasis on relationship management, complex planning, and AI-enabled service.

title: Pest control workers
rationale: Core tasks require travel, physical inspection of irregular spaces, pesticide application, trap placement, sealing barriers, and safe work around occupants, making them difficult to automate. AI can improve pest identification, treatment planning, estimates, routing, recordkeeping, and remote monitoring, but these remain supporting functions. Lower prices could expand preventive service and attract customers who currently tolerate pests or use do-it-yourself methods, although pest incidence and the need for onsite work limit demand growth. Because disruption remains low, the occupation is resilient.

title: Petroleum engineers
rationale: AI will materially accelerate reservoir modeling, production-data analysis, well design, equipment monitoring, and technical documentation. However, field-specific judgment, safety accountability, coordination with crews, and troubleshooting at remote well sites limit end-to-end automation of the core role. Demand is relatively inelastic because engineering costs are a small part of capital-intensive projects and oil and gas activity is governed mainly by commodity demand, geology, regulation, and energy investment, although geothermal and carbon-storage work may add some demand. Thus AI should enhance productivity and reduce some analytical workload without fully reshaping or replacing the occupation.

title: Pharmacists
rationale: AI and pharmacy automation can materially improve prescription verification, interaction screening, documentation, inventory management, billing, and routine patient counseling. However, licensed pharmacists remain responsible for safety oversight, complex clinical judgment, controlled dispensing, vaccinations, and direct collaboration with patients and healthcare teams. Demand is relatively inelastic because prescription volume is driven mainly by illness and prescribing patterns, although expanded medication-management services create some additional demand. The occupation is therefore resilient overall, with substantial task augmentation but continued need for accountable human professionals.

title: Pharmacy technicians
rationale: Prescription intake, data entry, insurance processing, customer routing, inventory management, and routine accuracy checks are structured tasks increasingly handled by AI-enabled pharmacy systems, while dispensing robots can automate counting, packaging, and labeling. Human technicians remain important for physical exception handling, compounding, hospital rounds, customer service, and regulatory oversight, limiting disruption below the very-high range. Demand for prescriptions will grow with population aging and chronic disease, but it is primarily driven by medical need rather than lower dispensing costs, so productivity gains are unlikely to produce enough additional volume to offset reduced labor per prescription.

title: Phlebotomists
rationale: The core work requires in-person venipuncture, dexterity, infection control, specimen handling, and reassurance of anxious patients, all of which remain difficult for AI without advanced and costly robotics. AI can streamline identity verification, labeling, documentation, scheduling, and error detection, but these are supporting rather than central tasks. Cheaper and faster collection could modestly expand preventive testing and access, but demand is constrained by clinical need and healthcare protocols, so phlebotomy remains resilient.

title: Photographers
rationale: Generative imagery, automated retouching, culling, tagging, marketing, and portfolio management will substantially change photographers’ workflows and displace some stock, product, and routine commercial photography. However, weddings, portraits, news events, and location-specific assignments still require physical presence, interpersonal skill, direction, and authentic documentation. Cheaper image production will expand visual-content demand, but much of that growth will be satisfied by synthetic images rather than additional photographers, yielding moderate elasticity and substantial restructuring rather than broad augmentation.

title: Physical therapist assistants and aides
rationale: Core duties require in-person patient observation, hands-on therapy, physical assistance, equipment setup, and interpersonal support, limiting AI substitution. AI can streamline documentation, scheduling, insurance forms, progress tracking, and exercise guidance, but these are peripheral or supervisory aids rather than replacements for direct care. Lower costs could unlock meaningful unmet rehabilitation demand, especially among older adults and people with chronic conditions, although insurance rules and the finite need for treatment constrain expansion. Consequently, AI will improve workflows without fundamentally reshaping most of the occupation, making it resilient.

title: Physical therapists
rationale: AI can streamline documentation, review medical histories, suggest care plans, and use computer vision or wearables to monitor exercises and progress. However, diagnosis through physical observation, hands-on therapy, safe patient movement, real-time adaptation, and interpersonal motivation still require substantial human presence and dexterity. Demand is relatively elastic because lower costs and greater availability could unlock considerable unmet rehabilitation, preventive-care, chronic-pain, and aging-related needs, but AI does not fundamentally replace the occupation's physical core, making it resilient.

title: Physician assistants
rationale: AI will materially assist with documentation, history review, diagnostic interpretation, treatment planning, and patient education. However, physical examinations, procedures, emergency judgment, patient relationships, and licensed clinical accountability require human presence, keeping disruption moderate. Demand is relatively elastic because aging populations, chronic disease, clinician shortages, and underserved communities create substantial unmet need that lower-cost care could unlock. The occupation is therefore resilient, with AI increasing PA capacity rather than replacing the hands-on clinical role.

title: Physicians and surgeons
rationale: AI will materially accelerate documentation, triage, diagnostic interpretation, treatment planning, and patient communication, with especially large effects in image- and data-intensive specialties. However, physical examination, procedures, surgery, emergency judgment, patient trust, team leadership, and legal accountability continue to require licensed physicians, limiting occupation-wide disruption. Lower costs could unlock meaningful unmet demand, particularly in primary care, mental health, and underserved communities, but insurance, regulation, training capacity, and the finite need for medical care constrain expansion. Because disruption remains moderate across this diverse occupation, AI is more likely to increase physician capacity and shift task composition than to reshape or replace the profession wholesale.

title: Physicists and astronomers
rationale: AI directly affects core tasks such as literature review, mathematical modeling, simulation, software development, data analysis, proposal drafting, and scientific writing. Human scientists remain essential for selecting consequential questions, validating novel theories, designing and operating specialized experiments, and exercising judgment when evidence is ambiguous. Faster research could support more hypotheses, analyses, and technology development, but demand is constrained by public research budgets, scarce facilities, long experimental cycles, and limited academic positions. The occupation therefore is likely to be substantially restructured around AI-enabled research rather than broadly replaced or expanded enough to qualify as augment.

title: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters
rationale: Core work requires physical presence, dexterity, tool use, and troubleshooting in varied and often confined environments, putting it largely beyond near-term AI automation. AI can assist with estimates, scheduling, code lookup, blueprint interpretation, BIM planning, and diagnostics, but these are secondary to installation and repair. Lower costs could stimulate some additional maintenance, renovations, and system upgrades, although demand remains constrained by the building stock, construction activity, and the frequency of failures. The low disruption score therefore makes the occupation resilient despite modest opportunities for demand expansion.

title: Podiatrists
rationale: AI can assist with imaging review, diagnostic support, documentation, treatment planning, and practice administration. However, physical examinations, procedures, surgery, orthotic fitting, and patient interaction require licensed clinicians with hands-on presence. Lower costs could unlock some preventive and diabetic foot care, but demand remains constrained by medical need, reimbursement, regulation, and substitution by other providers. Therefore, AI will improve podiatrists’ productivity without fundamentally replacing or reshaping the occupation’s core work.

title: Police and detectives
rationale: AI will materially assist with report writing, records searches, evidence review, video analysis, dispatch, and investigative lead generation. However, patrol, emergency response, interviews, arrests, conflict management, evidence collection, and courtroom testimony require physical presence, legal authority, and accountable human judgment. Demand is constrained by crime incidence, public-sector budgets, staffing rules, and community preferences, so cheaper administrative and analytical work is unlikely to produce proportionally more policing. The occupation is therefore resilient overall, although administrative workflows and some detective tasks will be substantially redesigned.

title: Political scientists
rationale: Political scientists perform predominantly digital and language-intensive work, including literature review, data analysis, policy evaluation, forecasting, monitoring, and report writing, all of which AI can substantially accelerate. Human judgment remains important for causal inference, political context, research design, sensitive advice, and stakeholder credibility, so full automation is unlikely. Demand may expand somewhat as cheaper analysis enables more policy scenarios and monitoring, but federal funding, institutional budgets, and a limited need for formal political research constrain that expansion. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore points to significant productivity-driven headcount pressure and a replace classification.

title: Postal service workers
rationale: Most postal work involves physical collection, handling, transport, and delivery in real-world environments, especially because mail carriers make up most employment. AI-enabled sorting, address recognition, route optimization, self-service, and customer-service tools will automate processing and allow larger delivery routes, but they will not eliminate the need for substantial physical labor within the next decade. Demand is highly inelastic because cheaper processing is unlikely to generate much more letter mail, although parcel delivery provides some support. The occupation is therefore resilient under the defined framework because disruption remains moderate, even though automation and declining mail volume will gradually reduce headcount.

title: Postsecondary education administrators
rationale: Much of the occupation consists of digital knowledge work—application review, records management, scheduling, compliance checks, data analysis, communications, and advising—that AI can automate or substantially accelerate. Leadership, sensitive student interactions, institutional accountability, recruitment travel, and crisis management still require human judgment and presence, preventing a higher disruption score. Demand is constrained by enrollment, institutional budgets, and a relatively fixed number of senior posts, so cheaper administration is unlikely to generate enough additional work to offset productivity gains, making headcount contraction likely, especially in admissions and registrar functions.

title: Postsecondary teachers
rationale: AI can materially automate lesson planning, content creation, routine grading, student feedback, literature reviews, data analysis, and parts of scholarly writing. Live instruction, mentoring, assessment integrity, laboratory supervision, original research, and institutional service still require substantial human judgment, presence, and accountability. Cheaper personalized instruction could expand access and course offerings, but enrollment, accreditation, public funding, credential demand, and the value placed on human faculty limit how much output growth translates into faculty jobs. The occupation therefore is likely to be restructured around AI-enabled teaching and research, with particular pressure on routine instruction and adjunct work.

title: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers
rationale: Core monitoring, forecasting, anomaly detection, equipment optimization, and grid-routing tasks are increasingly automatable through AI-enabled control systems and smart-grid technology. Safety-critical interventions, physical inspections, regulatory accountability, and emergency judgment will preserve a smaller cadre of highly trained human operators, preventing an even higher disruption score. Demand is inelastic because cheaper operation will not cause electricity consumption or the number of staffed control facilities to increase proportionally. High disruption combined with low elasticity therefore points to significant headcount contraction and a net effect of replacement.

title: Preschool and childcare center directors
rationale: AI can substantially streamline budgeting, scheduling, recordkeeping, compliance documentation, parent communications, staff training materials, and educational program planning. However, directors must remain onsite to supervise personnel, handle emergencies, maintain regulatory accountability, assess classrooms, and manage sensitive relationships with children, parents, and staff. Demand is relatively inelastic because each physical center generally needs accountable leadership, while enrollment, staffing ratios, low birth rates, and childcare costs constrain expansion. The occupation is therefore resilient: AI will alter and automate many administrative tasks but will not replace its core human leadership and onsite responsibilities.

title: Preschool teachers
rationale: The core work requires continuous in-person supervision, hands-on activities, emotional responsiveness, and management of unpredictable young children, all of which are difficult for AI to replace. AI can assist with lesson planning, developmental documentation, scheduling, and parent communications, but these are peripheral to classroom care and interaction. More affordable preschool could unlock meaningful demand among families currently constrained by cost or access, although child demographics, staffing ratios, and regulation limit expansion. The occupation is therefore resilient because AI will streamline administrative and planning tasks without substantially reshaping its human-centered core.

title: Private detectives and investigators
rationale: AI can substantially accelerate online-record searches, background checks, link analysis, video review, lead prioritization, and report drafting. However, interviews, covert surveillance, evidence collection, situational judgment, and legally compliant fieldwork still require human presence and accountability. Lower costs could unlock additional demand from individuals, small businesses, insurers, and attorneys, but privacy law, licensing, and the finite number of actionable cases limit expansion. Because AI reshapes the research and administrative portions without replacing the occupation's field-based core, the occupation is resilient.

title: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists
rationale: AI can substantially streamline report writing, case-file maintenance, risk assessment, resource matching, and electronic-monitoring review. However, core duties still require accountable human judgment, relationship building, court testimony, counseling, drug testing, and in-person visits in unpredictable or potentially dangerous settings. Cheaper service could support smaller caseloads and more intensive supervision, but demand is constrained by the number of people in correctional systems, legal requirements, and government budgets. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, the occupation is resilient even though its administrative workflow will change considerably.

title: Producers and directors
rationale: AI will materially accelerate script evaluation, budgeting, scheduling, casting searches, previsualization, editing, effects, and promotional work, while generative media will reshape production workflows. However, creative judgment, financing, leadership, actor direction, stakeholder management, and accountability on sets or stages remain strongly human-centered. Lower production costs should unlock many more niche, independent, advertising, streaming, and corporate productions, allowing expanded output to absorb much of the productivity gain and making augmentation the most likely net effect.

title: Project management specialists
rationale: AI can substantially automate project planning, scheduling, documentation, status reporting, budget monitoring, risk detection, and routine stakeholder communication. However, resolving ambiguous problems, negotiating tradeoffs, motivating teams, maintaining client trust, and bearing accountability still require significant human judgment. Cheaper project management may enable organizations to undertake more projects and give smaller initiatives access to formal coordination, but demand remains constrained by investment budgets and the capacity to execute projects. The occupation therefore will restructure around higher-level leadership, exception handling, and AI-enabled oversight, with fewer workers needed for coordination-heavy roles.

title: Property appraisers and assessors
rationale: Automated valuation models, computer vision, integrated property databases, and generative reporting can automate much of the comparable selection, valuation analysis, record verification, and report preparation that constitute the occupation's core knowledge work. Physical inspections, local knowledge, unusual properties, licensing requirements, and responsibility for defensible valuations preserve a meaningful human role, preventing an even higher disruption score. Demand is largely tied to property transactions, lending rules, taxation cycles, and disputes, so cheaper appraisals will generate only limited additional volume; consequently, productivity gains are likely to reduce headcount, especially in routine residential and mass-assessment work.

title: Property, real estate, and community association managers
rationale: AI can substantially automate listings, tenant communications, payment processing, recordkeeping, financial reporting, compliance checks, maintenance triage, and rent analysis. However, inspections, property showings, contractor supervision, emergency response, negotiation, and sensitive resident disputes still require local presence and human judgment. Demand is constrained by the property stock and number of communities, although lower management costs may encourage some owners to outsource and allow each manager to oversee more units, so the occupation is resilient but likely to become leaner and more technology-enabled.

title: Psychiatric technicians and aides
rationale: Core duties require continuous physical presence, interpersonal rapport, hands-on assistance, medication administration, and intervention with unpredictable or violent patients. AI can improve documentation, intake, behavioral monitoring, scheduling, and clinical alerts, but it cannot readily replace bedside supervision or physical care. Substantial unmet demand for mental health and substance-use treatment could absorb some productivity gains, although funding, facility capacity, regulation, and staffing requirements limit expansion. Because disruption remains low despite moderate demand elasticity, the occupation is resilient.

title: Psychologists
rationale: Psychology is predominantly cognitive and language-based, and AI can already support assessment, documentation, research synthesis, treatment planning, and routine therapeutic interactions. However, clinical judgment, trusted human rapport, observation of nuanced behavior, crisis management, and licensing requirements limit full automation. Demand is highly elastic because psychological services are constrained by cost, provider shortages, and limited access in schools and underserved communities. AI-enabled productivity should expand service capacity enough to support an augment outcome, while shifting psychologists toward complex cases, oversight, and relationship-intensive care.

title: Public relations and fundraising managers
rationale: AI can materially automate media monitoring, audience and donor analysis, message tailoring, grant drafting, press releases, speeches, and campaign reporting. However, reputation-sensitive judgment, crisis leadership, staff supervision, executive advising, event management, and personal relationships with journalists and major donors remain human-centered. Lower costs will enable more targeted campaigns and make sophisticated outreach accessible to smaller organizations, but donor resources, public attention, and the number of organizations needing senior managers limit demand expansion. The occupation therefore faces substantial skill and workflow changes without broad elimination, making restructure the best fit.

title: Public relations specialists
rationale: Most PR tasks—drafting releases, speeches, pitches, social posts, media monitoring, sentiment analysis, and campaign evaluation—are digital and already substantially accelerated by generative AI. Human judgment, trusted media relationships, executive counsel, and sensitive crisis response remain important, preventing near-total automation. Lower costs will enable more organizations and individuals to produce tailored communications and monitor reputational risks, but finite attention, organizational budgets, and the value of authentic relationships limit demand expansion. The occupation therefore will persist with fewer routine writing duties and greater emphasis on strategy, verification, relationship management, and crisis judgment.

title: Public safety telecommunicators
rationale: The occupation is almost entirely language- and computer-mediated, making call transcription, translation, location extraction, protocol-based triage, recordkeeping, and unit dispatch highly amenable to AI. Human judgment and empathy will remain important for ambiguous, emotionally charged, or life-threatening incidents, but AI can automate routine calls and let fewer telecommunicators supervise larger volumes. Demand is relatively inelastic because call volume is driven mainly by emergencies and population, while government budgets and required service coverage limit expansion. High disruption combined with low demand elasticity therefore points to substantial headcount pressure and a replace outcome.

title: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents
rationale: AI can automate much of the supplier research, proposal comparison, demand forecasting, contract review, order processing, and compliance monitoring that occupies procurement staff. Human judgment remains important for complex negotiations, supplier relationships, site inspections, exception handling, and accountability, preventing a very-high disruption score. Demand is constrained by organizations’ purchasing volumes and supplier networks, so cheaper procurement may enable more analysis and monitoring but is unlikely to generate proportionate growth in transactions. High disruption combined with low demand elasticity therefore points to headcount contraction, especially among routine purchasing-agent roles.

title: Quality control inspectors
rationale: AI-enabled machine vision, sensor analytics, and automated reporting directly target core inspection tasks such as detecting defects, comparing products with specifications, and accepting or rejecting items. Physical measurement, equipment setup, unusual materials, and investigation of ambiguous defects still require human presence, preventing an even higher disruption score. Demand for quality assurance may rise somewhat as cheaper systems enable continuous inspection, but inspection needs remain tied mainly to production volume and compliance requirements. Consequently, automation is likely to reduce routine inspector headcount while shifting remaining workers toward system oversight, exception handling, and root-cause analysis.

title: Radiation therapists
rationale: AI will increasingly assist with tumor localization, image guidance, machine calibration, safety checks, documentation, and patient monitoring. However, therapists must remain physically present to position and assist patients, operate regulated equipment, manage unexpected reactions, and provide compassionate care under strict clinical accountability. Demand is tied mainly to cancer incidence and prescribed treatment courses, while more efficient techniques may reduce the number of visits, so lower costs would produce only limited volume growth. The occupation is therefore resilient because AI will improve important workflows without removing its hands-on clinical core.

title: Radiologic and MRI technologists
rationale: AI can automate scan-protocol selection, image-quality checks, equipment calibration, records, and decisions about whether additional images are needed. However, the core work still requires in-person patient preparation, positioning, contrast administration, safety monitoring, and operation of large physical scanners, often with injured or anxious patients. Cheaper and faster imaging could unlock some additional demand, especially as the population ages, but clinical appropriateness rules, radiation exposure, scanner capacity, and reimbursement constraints limit expansion. The occupation is therefore resilient because AI will improve workflows without eliminating its hands-on core.

title: Railroad workers
rationale: AI and automation can improve routing, scheduling, equipment monitoring, inspections, and some locomotive or yard operations, but many core duties still require certified workers physically present in safety-critical environments. Freight and passenger rail demand is constrained by shipping volumes, infrastructure capacity, routes, and travel patterns, so cheaper labor inputs would generate only limited additional demand. Because regulation, legacy infrastructure, mechanical work, passenger interaction, and exception handling slow full autonomy, AI will alter workflows and crew sizes without broadly replacing the occupation over the next decade.

title: Real estate brokers and sales agents
rationale: AI can automate or greatly accelerate property matching, valuation, lead generation, marketing content, client communications, contract preparation, and transaction coordination. Human agents remain useful for property access, relationship-based selling, local judgment, negotiation, and handling unusual transactions, but these functions could be concentrated among fewer agents. Demand is relatively inelastic because transaction volume is constrained by housing supply, financing, mobility, and business needs rather than brokerage cost alone. High disruption combined with limited demand expansion therefore points to significant headcount contraction, especially in routine residential transactions.

title: Receptionists
rationale: AI voice agents, scheduling systems, digital check-in tools, and workflow automation can perform most phone handling, appointment management, information provision, message taking, and data entry. In-person greeting, security judgment, and assistance with difficult or unusual visitors remain human-intensive, especially in healthcare and complex facilities, but many employers can consolidate these duties into fewer roles. Demand is inelastic because organizations need only a limited volume of front-desk interactions, so cheaper service is unlikely to generate substantially more receptionist work. High disruption combined with low demand elasticity therefore points to significant headcount contraction and a net effect of replacement.

title: Recreation workers
rationale: Core duties require in-person leadership, supervision, motivation, safety monitoring, first aid, and adaptation to participants in unpredictable settings. AI can assist with scheduling, paperwork, promotion, activity planning, and suggested modifications, but it cannot readily replace the trusted physical presence central to the job. Lower administrative and planning costs could enable organizations to offer more programs, although budgets, facilities, staffing ratios, and participant availability limit expansion. Because disruption remains low despite moderate demand elasticity, the occupation is resilient.

title: Recreational therapists
rationale: AI can assist with patient-record review, treatment-plan drafting, activity customization, progress analysis, and clinical documentation. However, the core work depends on in-person observation, motivation, empathy, real-time adaptation, group facilitation, and sometimes physical assistance, limiting automation. Lower costs could unlock meaningful demand among older adults and people with mental health or rehabilitation needs, although reimbursement, facility funding, and staffing constraints would limit expansion. Because AI primarily improves planning and administration rather than replacing direct therapeutic engagement, the occupation is resilient.

title: Registered nurses
rationale: AI will materially assist with documentation, patient monitoring, care-plan preparation, clinical decision support, and patient education. However, bedside assessment, medication administration, equipment operation, physical assistance, emotional support, and emergency response require licensed human presence in unpredictable settings. Lower-cost nursing services could unlock additional preventive, chronic, elder, and home-based care, although reimbursement, staffing ratios, facilities, and licensing constrain expansion. Because AI reshapes important cognitive and administrative tasks without replacing the occupation’s hands-on core, registered nursing remains resilient.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
rationale: AI can substantially assist with assessments, rehabilitation-plan drafting, resource matching, documentation, progress monitoring, and routine client guidance. However, effective counseling still depends on human empathy, trust, nuanced observation, advocacy, and coordination across clients, families, employers, and healthcare professionals, often under licensing requirements. Demand has relatively high elasticity because disability and aging create substantial unmet need, although government budgets and reimbursement constraints will limit expansion. Because AI is likely to improve counselors’ capacity without fully reshaping the relationship-centered core, the occupation is resilient.

title: Respiratory therapists
rationale: AI can improve documentation, interpret pulmonary tests, optimize ventilator settings, and flag changes in patient status, but respiratory therapy remains centered on bedside examination, equipment setup, airway treatment, emergency response, and patient instruction. Demand could expand moderately through greater access to outpatient monitoring, home care, and preventive management, especially as the population ages, although disease incidence, clinical regulation, and the need for in-person care limit expansion. Because AI primarily supports rather than replaces the occupation’s hands-on clinical core, respiratory therapists are likely to remain resilient.

title: Retail sales workers
rationale: AI can automate product questions, recommendations, promotions, inventory lookup, and portions of checkout, while e-commerce and self-service systems reduce some routine customer interactions. However, much of the occupation still requires in-store presence, interpersonal persuasion, product demonstrations, loss awareness, stocking, and assistance with physical merchandise. Demand for retail goods is constrained by consumer income and underlying purchasing needs, so cheaper sales support is unlikely to generate enough additional purchases to offset major productivity gains. Because disruption remains moderate rather than high, the occupation is resilient under the specified thresholds, although routine positions are likely to face continued attrition.

title: Roofers
rationale: Roofing is overwhelmingly physical, site-specific work requiring climbing, balance, dexterity, material handling, and adaptation to irregular structures and weather conditions. AI may improve estimates, measurements, inspections, scheduling, and safety monitoring, but practical robotics are unlikely to replace crews broadly within the next decade. Demand has low elasticity because roof installation and replacement are driven mainly by building construction, damage, and finite maintenance cycles rather than by the cost of roofer labor alone. The occupation is therefore resilient, with AI affecting peripheral planning and administrative tasks more than its hands-on core.

title: Sales engineers
rationale: AI can materially accelerate product research, requirements analysis, proposal and presentation creation, solution configuration, demonstrations, and routine technical support. However, complex discovery, negotiation, customer trust, and coordination around high-value implementations still require human judgment and interpersonal skill. Lower-cost sales engineering could expand coverage to smaller accounts and support a growing range of sophisticated products, but demand remains constrained by the volume of business purchases and customers’ appetite for sales engagement. The occupation therefore is likely to restructure around AI-enabled productivity, consultative selling, and oversight of automated technical workflows rather than disappear.

title: Sales managers
rationale: AI can substantially automate sales forecasting, pipeline analysis, territory planning, reporting, training content, and performance monitoring, while also supporting customer outreach and complaint resolution. Human leadership, motivation, negotiation, accountability, and relationship management remain central, preventing near-total automation. Lower-cost analysis and coaching may let organizations pursue more customers and support larger sales operations, but each manager may also oversee more representatives, so demand expansion is only moderate. The role therefore persists but shifts toward strategic judgment, interpersonal leadership, and effective supervision of AI-enabled sales processes.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
rationale: AI can substantially automate career research, aptitude interpretation, academic planning, résumé support, recordkeeping, and identification of at-risk students. However, core school-counseling duties depend on trusted relationships, nuanced listening, crisis response, mandated reporting, and collaboration with families and staff, limiting end-to-end automation. Demand is highly latent because counseling caseloads are often large and personalized guidance is underprovided, although school budgets, credentialing, and institutional staffing constraints limit expansion. With disruption remaining just below the high-disruption threshold, AI is more likely to increase counselors’ capacity than fundamentally replace or restructure the occupation.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
rationale: Most core tasks—scheduling, correspondence, document preparation, transcription, record maintenance, and basic bookkeeping—are digital and increasingly automatable by AI agents integrated with office software. Human judgment, interpersonal coordination, and handling sensitive or specialized situations preserve some roles, especially in executive, medical, and legal settings. Demand has low elasticity because the amount of administrative support needed is largely determined by the number of executives, offices, patients, and transactions, while cheaper tools also enable other employees to perform these tasks themselves. High disruption combined with limited demand expansion makes replacement and substantial headcount consolidation the most likely net effect.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
rationale: Most market monitoring, securities analysis, valuation, trade execution, prospecting, and client communications are digital tasks that AI and automated platforms can perform or accelerate substantially. Human relationships, persuasion, accountability, licensing, and complex deal negotiation remain important, especially in investment banking and high-net-worth services, but they will support fewer agents equipped with stronger automation. Demand may expand somewhat as personalized financial guidance becomes cheaper, yet investable assets, transaction volume, regulation, and the finite supply of major deals limit that expansion, so productivity gains are likely to reduce headcount overall.

title: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
rationale: AI-enabled cameras, anomaly detection, automated access control, and report generation can substantially reduce routine monitoring work, especially for casino surveillance and stationary guards. However, patrols, visible deterrence, emergency response, confrontation management, and lawful detention still require unpredictable real-world presence and human judgment. Cheaper surveillance may encourage broader security coverage, but the need for protection at any given property is relatively fixed, so much of the productivity gain will reduce staffing per site rather than generate proportionate new demand. Because the occupation's physical response and public-facing duties keep overall disruption below the high-disruption threshold, it is classified as resilient despite likely restructuring and losses in monitoring-heavy roles.

title: Semiconductor processing technicians
rationale: AI-enabled machine vision, anomaly detection, process optimization, and predictive maintenance will automate substantial portions of monitoring, inspection, documentation, and parameter adjustment. However, technicians must still work onsite in cleanrooms to operate specialized equipment, troubleshoot physical processes, handle exceptions, and perform or coordinate repairs. Semiconductor demand is growing, but technician labor is a small share of fabrication costs, while capital capacity and lengthy plant construction constrain how much cheaper technician work can expand output. The occupation will evolve toward higher-level equipment oversight and troubleshooting, but its physical and site-specific core keeps disruption below the high-disruption threshold.

title: Set and exhibit designers
rationale: Generative design, image and 3D modeling tools, AI-assisted CAD, budgeting, and rapid visualization can materially accelerate concept development and revisions. However, designers still must interpret stakeholder goals, solve site-specific physical constraints, coordinate craftspeople, and oversee construction or installation. Lower design costs could enable more productions, exhibits, trade-show displays, and immersive experiences, but demand remains constrained by venue capacity and fabrication budgets. High disruption combined with moderate demand elasticity makes this a restructure occupation.

title: Sheet metal workers
rationale: Most core tasks require physical fabrication, material handling, installation, welding, and adaptation to varied construction sites, keeping them beyond the reach of near-term AI. AI-enabled CAD, automated cutting and bending equipment, and improved planning will affect shop fabrication and peripheral technical tasks, but not most fieldwork. Lower labor costs could encourage some additional HVAC retrofits and custom fabrication, although demand remains constrained by construction activity, material costs, and the finite number of buildings requiring work. The occupation is therefore resilient, with selective automation rather than wholesale transformation of its core.

title: Skincare specialists
rationale: Core tasks such as facials, waxing, skin preparation, sanitation, and massage require hands-on work, client presence, and careful physical execution. AI can improve skin analysis, product recommendations, appointment scheduling, marketing, and business administration, but it cannot readily perform most treatments without capable and affordable robotics. Demand is moderately elastic because skincare is discretionary and lower prices could attract more clients or increase visit frequency, although consumer time, trust, and local service capacity limit expansion. With disruption remaining low, the occupation is resilient despite meaningful opportunities for AI-assisted productivity.

title: Small engine mechanics
rationale: The occupation is dominated by hands-on inspection, disassembly, repair, calibration, and testing in varied physical environments, which current AI cannot perform without capable and economical robotics. AI can improve diagnostics, retrieve model-specific procedures, prepare estimates, communicate with customers, and automate recordkeeping, but these are supporting tasks. Cheaper and faster service could encourage customers to repair rather than replace equipment and obtain more preventive maintenance, although demand remains constrained by the installed equipment base and frequency of breakdowns. The low disruption score therefore makes the occupation resilient despite useful AI-enabled productivity gains.

title: Social and community service managers
rationale: AI can materially accelerate grant writing, reporting, budgeting, program evaluation, outreach content, and routine administrative coordination. However, the occupation’s core also depends on supervising staff, building community trust, negotiating with stakeholders, handling sensitive client and personnel issues, and maintaining accountable real-world leadership. Lower administrative costs could support more programs and larger caseloads, but demand is constrained by public and nonprofit funding, regulation, and organizational budgets. Because AI substantially assists but does not replace the human-centered managerial core, the occupation is resilient.

title: Social and human service assistants
rationale: AI can materially accelerate benefits research, eligibility screening, paperwork, documentation, translation, referrals, and routine client follow-up. However, assessing complex needs, building trust with vulnerable clients, handling crises, coordinating local providers, and conducting in-person visits require human judgment and presence. Lower costs could enable larger caseloads and more consistent outreach because social-service needs are substantially unmet, although government budgets, program eligibility, and limited service capacity constrain expansion. The occupation is therefore resilient: AI will alter many administrative tasks but is unlikely to reshape or absorb the human-centered core.

title: Social workers
rationale: AI can substantially streamline documentation, benefit and resource matching, case monitoring, treatment-plan drafting, and routine client communication. However, crisis intervention, safeguarding decisions, psychotherapy, field visits, advocacy, and trust-building require human judgment, accountability, and interpersonal presence. Demand is highly latent because of large caseloads and unmet mental-health and social-service needs, although licensing rules and public-budget constraints limit expansion. Because AI reshapes supporting tasks more than the relationship-centered core, the occupation remains resilient while becoming significantly more productive.

title: Sociologists
rationale: Much of sociologists' work—literature review, survey design, statistical analysis, qualitative coding, and report writing—is cognitive and directly affected by AI. Human expertise remains important for selecting valid research questions, interpreting social context, conducting sensitive fieldwork, and advising stakeholders. Lower research costs could enable more organizations to commission sociological analysis, but demand is constrained by government, academic, and nonprofit budgets rather than purely by price. The occupation therefore is likely to restructure around AI-enabled research workflows, methodological oversight, and high-level interpretation rather than experience either wholesale replacement or enough expansion to offset all productivity gains.

title: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
rationale: Nearly all core tasks—requirements analysis, coding, documentation, debugging, test generation, and maintenance—are digital and increasingly accelerated or partially automated by AI tools. Demand is highly elastic because cheaper software development enables more applications, customization, automation, connected products, and security systems, although organizational constraints prevent output from expanding in direct proportion to productivity. The occupation will change substantially, with routine coding and manual testing declining while architecture, validation, security, integration, and stakeholder work gain importance, but strong latent demand should keep aggregate employment stable or growing.

title: Solar photovoltaic installers
rationale: Core tasks require physical presence, rooftop mobility, tool use, electrical connections, and adaptation to varied structures and site conditions, keeping direct AI disruption low. AI can improve system configuration, measurements, permitting, scheduling, diagnostics, and training, but practical jobsite robotics remain difficult over the next decade. Demand is highly elastic because lower installation costs would accelerate solar adoption, although hardware, grid, permitting, and property constraints limit it somewhat; with disruption below 7, the occupation is resilient.

title: Special education teachers
rationale: AI can substantially streamline IEP drafting, lesson adaptation, assessment analysis, progress documentation, and creation of personalized learning materials. However, the core work depends on in-person observation, relationship-building, behavioral support, safeguarding, and responsive instruction for students with diverse and sometimes severe disabilities. Cheaper personalization could improve service intensity and reach more underserved students, but enrollment, legal requirements, staffing ratios, and public-school budgets limit demand expansion. Because AI reshapes supporting knowledge tasks without replacing the human-centered core, the occupation is resilient.

title: Special effects artists and animators
rationale: Animation and visual-effects production is almost entirely digital, and generative AI already accelerates concept art, modeling, rigging, in-betweening, compositing, and revision workflows. Human artistic direction, narrative judgment, consistency, and collaboration remain important, but the production pipeline and required technical skills will change substantially. Lower costs should unlock more animation and effects for games, advertising, independent media, mobile applications, and personalized content, although audience attention and major-studio budgets limit expansion. The high disruption combined with substantial latent demand makes augment the best fit, with workers producing far more output while routine production roles face pressure.

title: Speech-language pathologists
rationale: AI can automate documentation, analyze speech patterns, support screening, generate treatment plans, and deliver adaptive practice exercises, materially changing the digital and language-based portions of the job. However, diagnosis and therapy still depend heavily on clinical judgment, patient rapport, family counseling, real-time behavioral observation, and hands-on swallowing assessment. Demand is relatively elastic because lower-cost teletherapy and AI-supported care could expand access amid provider shortages, although licensing, reimbursement, and school budgets limit expansion. Because AI substantially assists but does not fully reshape the human-centered clinical core, the occupation remains resilient.

title: Stationary engineers and boiler operators
rationale: AI-enabled controls, predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, and automated logging will materially improve monitoring, diagnostics, and operating efficiency. However, physical inspections, repairs, emergency response, safety accountability, and work in hazardous equipment spaces still require skilled on-site workers. Demand is tied to the fixed number of facilities and utility systems rather than the price of operator labor, so productivity gains will create little additional work; nevertheless, the occupation remains resilient because its hands-on core limits disruption.

title: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors
rationale: Counseling is predominantly language- and knowledge-based, so AI can materially assist with screening, documentation, treatment planning, routine coaching, progress monitoring, and between-session support. However, therapeutic trust, nuanced assessment, crisis intervention, accountability, and licensed clinical judgment will continue to require substantial human involvement. Demand is highly elastic because mental health and addiction services are severely capacity-constrained and often unaffordable, so lower costs and greater productivity would unlock extensive unmet demand. High disruption combined with very high elasticity therefore points to augmentation rather than broad counselor replacement.

title: Surgical assistants and technologists
rationale: Core tasks are hands-on, time-critical, and performed in a sterile, unpredictable operating-room environment, including positioning patients, passing instruments, maintaining sterility, and directly assisting with incisions or closure. AI may improve equipment setup, inventory tracking, documentation, robotic-system support, and procedural guidance, but replacing the required dexterity and physical presence would require major advances in robotics. Demand is relatively inelastic because surgical volume is constrained by medical need, reimbursement, facility capacity, and the availability of surgeons, although lower costs could modestly expand elective and outpatient procedures. The occupation is therefore resilient because AI will mainly enhance peripheral and coordination tasks rather than reshape its physical core.

title: Survey researchers
rationale: Survey research is predominantly digital and cognitive, and AI can already accelerate background research, questionnaire drafting, statistical coding, data analysis, visualization, and report writing. Human expertise remains important for sampling strategy, bias and nonresponse correction, instrument validity, fieldwork oversight, and defensible interpretation. Lower costs will enable more frequent and accessible research, but respondent availability, data quality, institutional budgets, and competition from behavioral and administrative data limit demand expansion. Thus, the occupation will persist with fewer routine tasks and a stronger emphasis on methodology, quality assurance, and strategic interpretation.

title: Surveying and mapping technicians
rationale: AI, computer vision, drones, and automated GIS tools will substantially accelerate image processing, feature extraction, calculations, database maintenance, and map production. However, much of the occupation still requires travel, instrument operation, marker placement, equipment troubleshooting, and judgment in unpredictable outdoor environments. Cheaper geospatial data will support additional mapping for infrastructure, utilities, development, and environmental monitoring, although demand remains partly constrained by the number of physical projects and legally required surveys. Because AI significantly improves the office-based portion without eliminating the field-based core, the occupation is resilient rather than highly disrupted.

title: Surveyors
rationale: AI can accelerate title research, data validation, point-cloud interpretation, mapping, CAD/GIS production, and report preparation, while drones and robotic instruments further automate data collection. However, substantial fieldwork, site-specific judgment, discrepancy resolution, legal certification, and licensed accountability remain difficult to automate fully. Demand is tied mainly to property transactions, construction, infrastructure, mining, and regulatory requirements, so lower costs may increase survey scope and frequency but are unlikely to produce a proportional surge in projects. The occupation is therefore resilient, although productivity gains may limit headcount growth and shift work toward oversight, interpretation, and certification.

title: Tax examiners and collectors, and revenue agents
rationale: Most return review, document analysis, liability calculation, case prioritization, recordkeeping, and taxpayer correspondence are structured digital tasks that AI can substantially automate. Human judgment, legal accountability, sensitive negotiations, investigations, and field audits remain important, especially for complex or contested cases. Although cheaper enforcement could enable governments to examine more questionable returns, demand is constrained by the finite tax base, statutory processes, enforcement priorities, and public budgets, so productivity gains are likely to reduce headcount and concentrate remaining workers on complex cases.

title: Taxi drivers, shuttle drivers, and chauffeurs
rationale: Driving is physical and requires real-world judgment, but autonomous-vehicle AI directly targets the occupation’s core task and is already operating in limited, geofenced markets. Adoption over the next decade will remain constrained by weather, complex roads, regulation, liability, and passenger needs such as luggage or wheelchair assistance, so disruption will be substantial but uneven. Much cheaper rides would generate additional trips, especially among older adults, people with disabilities, and households without cars, but travel-time and congestion constraints limit demand expansion. The occupation therefore restructures toward assisted transportation, premium service, supervision, and difficult routes while routine urban trips increasingly become automated.

title: Teacher assistants
rationale: AI can materially assist with lesson reinforcement, personalized exercises, progress tracking, grading, and recordkeeping. However, much of the occupation requires in-person supervision, behavior management, relationship building, and hands-on support for young or disabled students. Demand for individualized instruction could expand, but enrollment, staffing budgets, and the need for physical coverage limit that expansion. Because AI changes the instructional and administrative portions without replacing the occupation’s presence-dependent core, the occupation is resilient.

title: Technical writers
rationale: Technical writing is predominantly digital and language-based, and AI can already draft, revise, summarize, translate, standardize, and reformat documentation from source materials.
